source.title: Explaining grokking through circuit efficiency
source.authors: Vikrant Varma; Rohin Shah; Zachary Kenton; J'anos Kram'ar; Ramana Kumar

record.tranche_reason: The study trains models on modular arithmetic and tests grokking-related predictions, but its principal measures and interventions concern circuit efficiency, reduced-data retraining, and circuit-strength proxies rather than a direct reproduction of the original study.
record.gate_note: The paper also discusses results from prior work, including progress measures reported by Nanda et al. Those cited results are not rows. The rows below use this paper's own experiments and reported outcomes.
record.test_reason: The authors train 1-layer Transformers on modular arithmetic and group tasks. They test their own efficiency explanation of grokking (V5) through four predictions: efficiency versus dataset size, ungrokking phase transition, weight-decay independence, and semi-grokking. They also report standard grokking curves (V1) and circuit-strength proxies over training (V2). This is a different method aimed at the original question of why grokking happens.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that grokking occurs because the generalising circuit is more efficient but slower to learn than memorisation, so weight decay reallocates norm to it. A critical dataset size follows, and they confirm their predictions of ungrokking and semi-grokking. They acknowledge the account relies on weight decay and is incomplete without it, and that Dcrit is an oversimplification. They remain confident it is at least part of the explanation when weight decay is present.
record.recipe_differences: Uses 1-layer decoder-only Transformers trained with AdamW on modular arithmetic, and investigates circuit-efficiency predictions, reduced-data retraining, and circuit-logit proxies rather than directly replicating the original study's complete method.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported critical dataset size varies with random initialization and training dynamics. Weight decay is varied; the paper reports that the ungrokking transition and final accuracy are largely independent of it in the tested settings. Circuit-proxy measurements also have stated limitations.
record.problems: The paper reports significant variation across random seeds; its circuit-strength measures are indirect and acknowledged to overestimate the generalizing contribution and underestimate the memorizing contribution. The semi-grokking result is difficult to demonstrate and includes a cherry-picked detailed example. Many plotted results have no numerical values or uncertainty estimates in the text. The authors acknowledge that their weight-decay account does not explain grokking observed without weight decay.

untested.parts: That the delay grows as the training set shrinks is not measured; it is cited from Power et al. (super-exponential growth).
No causal ablation of circuits. Strengths come from logit-projection proxies on a single randomly picked run. There is no test that the proxies anticipate the jump across runs.
No non-algorithmic data and no initialisation-scale manipulation; Liu et al. (2023) is only discussed.
No test of the account without weight decay or with other low-norm biases. The authors speculate that implicit regularisation plays this role.
Not tested. Seed variance in efficiency is speculatively attributed to different key frequencies or circuits.
Optimizer and numerical artifacts are not controlled; all runs use AdamW. The authors only remark that most of their runs show no slingshots.

missing.what: Single semi-grokking run converging to 83% test accuracy
Ungrokking example curve, and the sweep over 7 dataset sizes in [390, 1494] with 10 seeds each. Small sizes ungrok to poor accuracy and intermediate sizes to middling accuracy.
Semi-grokking reaches about 0.7 test accuracy at about 2000 examples, while ungrokking reaches about 0.7 at about 800–1000 examples. So the effective Dcrit depends on initialisation.
Toy simulation: no grokking when the generalising circuit is less efficient or is learned as fast as the memorising one

record.verdict_notes: Not an original source. The V2 evidence rests on a single run with self-described biased proxies: the generalising strength is overestimated and memorisation underestimated. The study gives no uncertainty estimates. The record's V2 limits_scope label (r6) was dropped because it rested on proxy caveats rather than on a result.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not directly test whether the grokking delay grows as the training set shrinks. It reports a standard grokking run and semi-grokking runs, but the latter reach partial rather than near-perfect test accuracy.

Circuit strengths are estimated using imperfect logit proxies, not direct measurements of circuit removal or causal contribution. The paper does not establish that these measures reliably anticipate the test-accuracy jump across runs.
Non-algorithmic data and initialization-scale or weight-norm switches are discussed through cited work, not tested here.
No LLM pretraining or fine-tuning on realistic data is tested.

The proposed critical dataset size is not established as a universal threshold; the study reports that initialization and training dynamics affect it. The paper does not test a general prediction that a threshold exists across realistic tasks.
The study does not identify and compare the algorithms reached across runs. It speculates that different key frequencies or circuits may account for observed efficiency variation.
Adaptive-optimizer instabilities and floating-point limits in the softmax are not tested as explanations.

rows.subject: 1-layer decoder-only Transformer
rows.operation_detail: Train on modular addition and track training and test performance
rows.measure: Training accuracy, training and test loss, parameter norm, and trigonometric and memorization correct-logit proxies over training
rows.value: By step 200, training accuracy is perfect; test loss starts falling at step 3500, and the paper reports good generalization by step 6000.
rows.note: The reported late improvement follows perfect training accuracy, but the account gives no numerical final test accuracy for this run.
rows.check: Should be observed, not partial. Training accuracy is perfect by step 200, test loss falls from step 3500, and generalisation is good by step 6000. Figure 1a also states 100% test accuracy for the D≫Dcrit run, so the final accuracy is given. Add Figure 1a to the locator.

rows.subject: 1-layer decoder-only Transformer
rows.operation_detail: Train from random initialization while sweeping training dataset size

conditions.value: 20 evenly spaced sizes in [1500, 2050], 10 seeds each

rows.measure: Test accuracy over training; count of runs showing clear semi-grokking
rows.value: At least 6 of 200 runs show clear semi-grokking; many other runs show transient middling test accuracy or multiple plateaus before full generalization.
rows.note: The reported semi-grokking is delayed generalization to middling accuracy, not the near-perfect test accuracy described in V1.
rows.check: Partial is correct for V1: generalisation is delayed but reaches only middling accuracy. For V5, semi-grokking is the authors' prediction P4, so the same result confirms V5. The single state hides this difference between versions.

source_check.correct: V1: partial within the reported training budget. V5: observed; semi-grokking confirms prediction P4.
source_check.problem: The shared partial state does not fit both linked versions.

rows.subject: 1-layer decoder-only Transformer
rows.operation_detail: Train from random initialization on a reduced modular-addition dataset
rows.measure: Training and test accuracy over training
rows.value: At epoch 0.8 × 10^7, test accuracy rises to around 0.55 and stays there for 10^7 epochs; at epoch 1.8 × 10^7 it rises to 1.
rows.note: The paper describes this as transient semi-grokking and says it is a cherry-picked example.
rows.check: Single cherry-picked run. The plateau at about 0.55 is transient, and the run later reaches test accuracy 1 at 1.8e7 epochs. For V5 this is the predicted transient semi-grokking, not a weakened effect.

source_check.correct: V1: partial during the intermediate plateau, followed by full generalization at epoch 1.8 × 10^7. V5: observed transient semi-grokking.
source_check.problem: The shared partial state obscures confirmation of V5 and the eventual perfect endpoint.

rows.subject: 1-layer decoder-only Transformer
rows.operation_detail: Track the correct-logit proxy for the trigonometric generalizing circuit
rows.value: The trigonometric logit grows during training and becomes higher than the memorization logit by step 1500.
rows.note: This is a proxy obtained by projecting logits into a trigonometric subspace.

rows.subject: 1-layer decoder-only Transformer
rows.operation_detail: Track the correct-logit proxy for the memorization circuit
rows.value: The memorization logit is about 0 by step 4000.
rows.note: The paper interprets the pattern as consistent with weakening memorization, while cautioning that its proxy measures can underestimate memorization.

rows.subject: 1-layer decoder-only Transformer
rows.value: Parameter norm falls while both circuit-logit proxies rise from epochs 200 to 1500; after epoch 4000 the trigonometric logit falls while test loss continues to fall.
rows.note: The authors say the proxies have flaws and suggest the late test-loss decline may reflect cleanup of incorrect memorization logits.
rows.check: Parameter norm falls while the generalising (trig) logit rises, before test loss drops. The later fall in the trig logit coincides with the authors' cleanup interpretation and does not contradict the gradual mechanism. Observed rather than partial; the proxy caveat is a measurement limitation, not a weaker effect.

conditions.value: from a generalization-only network trained on the full dataset

rows.measure: Generalization-to-memorization correct-logit ratio and test accuracy at convergence
rows.value: The logit ratio changes monotonically over 6 orders of magnitude with dataset size; test accuracy has a smooth dependence on dataset size. The authors say initialization and training dynamics affect the dataset size at which middling generalization occurs.
rows.note: The authors call Dcrit an oversimplification because the initialisation and training dynamics affect which circuits are found.
